   364	
   365	    # Momentum tendency
   366	    du_dt_3d = -grad_B_3d - pg_corr_3d + pv_flux_3d  # (nEdges, nlev)
   367	
   368	    # Viscosity — when both del2 and del4 are active, the biharmonic
   369	    # ``vector_laplacian_del4_3d`` is defined as
   370	    # ``-vector_laplacian_del2_3d(vector_laplacian_del2_3d(u))``, so
   371	    # the *inner* del2 is identical to the explicit del2 viscosity.
   372	    # Compute it once and reuse — saves one full
   373	    # ``vector_laplacian_del2_3d`` call (1 div + 1 curl + 1 grad +
   374	    # 1 tangential-curl difference) per RHS evaluation.  Same exploit
   375	    # as Loop 135 for the latlon ocean K_h+K_bih sharing.
   376	    if config.nu_del2 > 0 and config.nu_del4 > 0:
   377	        _del2_u = vector_laplacian_del2_3d(u_3d, mesh)
   378	        du_dt_3d = du_dt_3d + config.nu_del2 * _del2_u
   379	        du_dt_3d = du_dt_3d - config.nu_del4 * vector_laplacian_del2_3d(_del2_u, mesh)
   380	    elif config.nu_del2 > 0:
   381	        du_dt_3d = du_dt_3d + config.nu_del2 * vector_laplacian_del2_3d(u_3d, mesh)
   382	    elif config.nu_del4 > 0:

   386	    # MPAS edgesOnCell gather + reduce on the leading edge axis (the
   387	    # trailing nlev axis is purely passive), so all the divergences
   388	    # the dycore needs at this stage can fold into a single call:
   389	    #
   390	    #   * div(u)                 — horizontal-advection / PV bookkeeping
   391	    #   * div(u * T_edge)        — temperature flux divergence
   392	    #   * div(u * ln_ps_edge)    — v·∇(ln p_s) thermodynamic correction
   393	    #   * div(u * dp_edge)       — flux-form layer-mass continuity
   394	    #                              (BOTH branches; σ uses dp = p_s_edge·Δσ)
   395	    #   * div(grad_T)            — K_h scalar Laplacian (only when ``K_h > 0``)
   396	    #
   397	    # Pull ``ln_ps_edge`` and (when hybrid) ``u*dp_edge_3d`` and (when
   398	    # K_h > 0) ``grad_T_3d_pre`` up into the batch so the standalone
   399	    # divergence calls that previously fired later in the function are
   400	    # eliminated.
   401	    flux_T_3d = u_3d * T_edge_3d  # (nEdges, nlev)
   402	    # ``ln_ps_edge_pre`` was already produced by the batched
   403	    # ``cell_to_edge_avg_3d`` block above (Loop 175); reuse it here so
   404	    # the standalone 2D ``cell_to_edge_avg(ln_ps)`` call is eliminated.

   407	    n_edges_d, nlev_d = u_3d.shape

   409	    _div_input_list = [u_3d, flux_T_3d, flux_lnps_3d]

   411	    _idx_gradT = -1

   415	    _idx_udp = len(_div_input_list) - 1
   416	    if config.K_h > 0:
   417	        _div_input_list.append(grad_T_3d_pre)
   418	        _idx_gradT = len(_div_input_list) - 1

   420	    _n_div = len(_div_input_list)
   421	    _div_inputs = jnp.stack(_div_input_list, axis=-1)  # (nEdges, nlev, K)
   422	    _div_outputs = divergence_cell_3d(
   423	        _div_inputs.reshape(n_edges_d, nlev_d * _n_div), mesh,

   426	    div_uT_3d = _div_outputs[..., _idx_uT]
   427	    div_flux_lnps = _div_outputs[..., _idx_ulnps]
   428	    div_dp_3d = _div_outputs[..., _idx_udp]  # flux-form div(u·dp), both branches

   432

   438	    # --- 4. Surface pressure tendency and vertical velocity ---

   441	    # ``dp_s_dt`` (last entry) and the σ̇ / mass-flux integration (iter-53/54

   443	    # divergence (mass export) ⇒ dp_s/dt < 0.

   448	        #   B_range * dp_s/dt = -sum_k div(dp_k * v_k)
   449	        dp_s_dt = -_D_total_p[..., 0] / sigma_coord.B_range
   450	
   451	        # Flux-form mass flux from the SAME cumsum — consistent with the
   452	        # flux-form dp_s_dt above.  (compute_mass_flux_hybrid would rebuild
   453	        # it from the ADVECTIVE div(v)·dp, which differs wherever ∇p_s ≠ 0.)
   454	        mass_flux = compute_mass_flux_from_cumsum(
   455	            _cumsum_dp, _D_total_p, sigma_coord,
   456	        )
   457	        # θ-form vertical thermodynamic transport (cancellation-free, #930):
   458	        #   -F·∂T/∂p + κ·T·F/p  ==  -exner·F·∂θ/∂p   (θ = T·(p₀/p)^κ).
   459	        # Advecting θ cancels the two large near-equal terms BEFORE
   460	        # discretization, killing the 2Δz residual the 1/p prefactor
   461	        # amplified at the stretched top levels.  See the σ branch below.

   463	            T_3d, mass_flux, p_s, sigma_coord)

   465	        #   ω = B·dp_s/dt + F  ⇒  ω_ps = B·dp_s/dt.  The F (mass-flux) part
   466	        # κ·T·F/p is now folded into ``vert_thermo_T`` above — NO double-count.
   467	        omega_ps = sigma_coord.B_full * dp_s_dt[:, None]
   468	    else:
   469	        sigma_top = sigma_coord.sigma_half[0]
   470	        sigma_range = 1.0 - sigma_top
   471	
   472	        # σ closure: (1 - σ_top)·dp_s/dt = -Σ_k div(u·p_s_edge·Δσ_k).
   473	        # ``div_dp`` already carries the p_s factor (flux form) — no extra
   474	        # p_s multiply, unlike the old advective div(v)·Δσ closure.
   475	        dp_s_dt = -_D_total_p[..., 0] / sigma_range
   476	
   477	        # Flux-form σ̇ from the SAME cumsum (shared closure; mirrors the
   478	        # lat-lon C-grid reference implementation).
   479	        sigma_dot = compute_sigma_dot_from_cumsum(
   480	            _cumsum_dp, _D_total_p, p_s, sigma_coord,
   481	        )
   482	
   483	        # θ-form vertical thermodynamic transport (cancellation-free, #930):
   484	        #   -σ̇·∂T/∂σ + κ·T·σ̇/σ  ==  -exner·σ̇·∂θ/∂σ   (θ = T·(p₀/p)^κ).
   485	        # The split form computes -σ̇·∂T/∂σ (first-diff, ×2 at the 2Δz
   486	        # Nyquist) and κ·T·σ̇/σ (point value, ×1) separately, leaving a
   487	        # spurious 2Δz residual that the 1/σ prefactor amplifies at the
   488	        # stretched top levels.  Advecting θ cancels the two large terms

   490	        # is inherited verbatim from the reused ``vertical_advection``.
   491	        vert_thermo_T = vertical_advection_theta(
   492	            T_3d, sigma_dot, p_s, sigma_coord)
   493	        # Only the surface-pressure-tendency part of ω stays in ``adiabatic``:
   494	        #   ω = σ·dp_s/dt + p_s·σ̇  ⇒  ω_ps = σ·dp_s/dt.  The σ̇ part
   495	        # κ·T·σ̇/σ is now folded into ``vert_thermo_T`` above — NO double-count.
   496	        omega_ps = sigma_coord.sigma_full * dp_s_dt[:, None]

   499	    if config.nu_del4_ps > 0:
   500	        del2_ps = divergence_cell(gradient_edge(p_s, mesh), mesh)
   525	
   526	    # v·∇(ln p_s) at cells: div(u * ln_ps_edge) - ln_ps * div(u).
   527	    # ``div_flux_lnps`` was already computed via the batched divergence
   528	    # block above; just combine it with ``div_3d`` here.
   529	    v_grad_lnps = div_flux_lnps - ln_ps[:, None] * div_3d  # (nCells, nlev)

   532	    # so the adiabatic correction needs the same factor.
   533	    if _hybrid:
   534	        v_grad_lnps = v_grad_lnps * (sigma_coord.B_full * p_s[:, None] / p_adiab)

   537	    dT_dt_3d = horiz_adv_T_3d + vert_thermo_T + adiabatic
   538	
   539	    # Vertical biharmonic hyperdiffusion of T (#930 cure): damp the grid-scale
   540	    # 2Δσ vertical mode that the adiabatic κ·T·ω/p term amplifies but no other
   541	    # vertical operator in this dycore opposes.  Zero when nu_vert4_T == 0.
   542	    if config.nu_vert4_T > 0.0 and T_3d.shape[-1] > 2:
   543	        dT_dt_3d = dT_dt_3d + vertical_del4_T_tendency(T_3d, config.nu_vert4_T)
   544	
   545	    # --- 6. Add physics tendencies ---
   546	    if physics_tendency is not None:
   547	        du_dt_3d = du_dt_3d + physics_tendency.du_dt.data
   548	        dT_dt_3d = dT_dt_3d + physics_tendency.dT_dt.data
   549	        dp_s_dt = dp_s_dt + physics_tendency.dp_s_dt.data
   550	
   551	    # --- 7. Tracer transport (moisture etc.) ---
   552	    # Advect prognostic tracers with the dycore's OWN edge wind (u_3d) and
   553	    # vertical mass flux (mass_flux for hybrid / sigma_dot for σ), so moisture
   554	    # transport is MASS-CONSISTENT with the thermodynamics — same horizontal
   555	    # operator (shared ``tracer_horizontal_advection``) and the SAME vertical
   556	    # operator the dycore uses for T.  Physics (microphysics/convection)
   557	    # tracer tendencies add on.  ``tracers=None`` ⇒ dry, no extra work.
   558	    tracer_tends_out = None

   560	        from legoesm.atmosphere.dynamics.gcm.tracer_transport_mpas import (
   561	            tracer_horizontal_advection,
   562	        )
   563	        _tnames = list(state.tracers.keys())
   564	        q = jnp.stack([state.tracers[k].data for k in _tnames], axis=-1)

   567	            dq = dq + jax.vmap(
   568	                lambda qk: vertical_advection_hybrid(qk, mass_flux, p_s, sigma_coord),
   569	                in_axes=-1, out_axes=-1)(q)
   570	        else:
   571	            dq = dq + jax.vmap(
   572	                lambda qk: vertical_advection(qk, sigma_dot, sigma_coord),
   573	                in_axes=-1, out_axes=-1)(q)

   575	        # as the T filter above).  The 2026-07-23 moist-AMIP blowup forensics
   576	        # (Tibetan-plateau cell, ±140 K 2Δσ T zigzag with 66 g/kg q_v pooling
   577	        # at the hot levels) show the moist checkerboard's primary oscillator
   578	        # is the TRACER field: tracer vertical transport reuses the
   579	        # checkerboard-prone ``vertical_advection`` form (only T got the #962
   580	        # θ-form rewrite), so damping T alone cannot stabilize the coupled
   581	        # q↔latent-heating mode.  Column-integral ZERO by the same no-flux

   583	        # to machine precision.  Zero when nu_vert4_T == 0 (bit-identical).
   584	        if config.nu_vert4_T > 0.0 and q.shape[-2] > 2:
   585	            dq = dq + jax.vmap(
   586	                lambda qk: vertical_del4_T_tendency(qk, config.nu_vert4_T),
   587	                in_axes=-1, out_axes=-1)(q)
   588	        _phys_tt = (physics_tendency.tracer_tendencies
   589	                    if physics_tendency is not None else None)
   590	        for _i, k in enumerate(_tnames):
   591	            if _phys_tt is not None and k in _phys_tt:
   592	                dq = dq.at[..., _i].add(_phys_tt[k].data)
   593	        tracer_tends_out = {
   594	            k: Field(data=dq[..., _i], name=f"d{k}_dt",
   595	                     dims=("nCells", "nlev"), units="kg/kg/s")
   195	    return None
   196	
   197	
   198	class DiagnosticCollector:
   199	    """Accumulates diagnostics during a simulation.
   200	
   201	    Manages time-series arrays, vertical profiles, 2D snapshots,
   202	    energy budget tracking, and optional monthly-mean accumulation.
   203	
   204	    Parameters
   205	    ----------
   206	    nlev : int
   207	        Number of vertical levels.
   208	    sigma_full : array
   209	        Sigma at full levels.
   210	    dsigma : array
   211	        Layer thickness in sigma.
   212	    monthly_means : bool
   213	        Enable monthly-mean zonal diagnostics.
   214	    cmip_output : bool
   215	        Enable CF/CMOR NetCDF output.
   216	    clear_sky_diag : bool
   217	        Track clear-sky radiation diagnostics.
   218	    n_days : int
   219	        Total simulation days (for snapshot selection).
   220	    output_dir : str or Path
   221	        Output directory for diagnostics and CMOR files.
   222	    """
   223	
   224	    def __init__(
   225	        self,
   226	        nlev: int,
   227	        sigma_full,
   228	        dsigma,
   229	        experiment_id: str = "amip",
   230	        monthly_means: bool = False,
   231	        cmip_output: bool = False,
   232	        clear_sky_diag: bool = False,
   233	        n_days: int = 200,
   234	        output_dir: str | Path = "",
   235	        cmip_resolution_deg: float = 5.0,
   236	        start_year: int = 1979,
   237	        cloud_config=None,
   238	    ):
   239	        self.nlev = nlev
   240	        self.sigma_full = sigma_full
   241	        self.dsigma = dsigma
   242	        self.clear_sky_diag = clear_sky_diag
   243	        # Cloud config (``atmosphere.physics.clouds.CloudConfig`` or ``None``)
   244	        # for the total-cloud-cover ``clt`` diagnostic — the SAME scheme
   245	        # selection radiation uses, so ``clt`` reflects the model's actual
   535	            # flattened (nCells*nlev,) inputs are not supported here.
   536	            return self._roll_to_cmip_lon(
   537	                apply_voronoi_to_latlon_3d(arr, self._voronoi_regrid_weights))
   538	        arr = np.asarray(field)
   539	        if arr.ndim == 3:
   540	            regrid = getattr(self, '_structured_regrid', None)
   541	            if regrid is not None:
   542	                return _apply_structured_regrid_3d(arr, regrid)
   543	            # Resample when source shape differs from CMIP target
   544	            if arr.shape[:2] != (self._cmip_nlat, self._cmip_nlon):
   545	                from scipy.ndimage import zoom
   546	                factors = (self._cmip_nlat / arr.shape[0],
   547	                           self._cmip_nlon / arr.shape[1],
   548	                           1.0)
   549	                return zoom(arr, factors, order=1)
   550	            return arr
   551	        return None
   552	
   553	    def _interp_to_plev19(self, field_3d, p_s) -> np.ndarray | None:
   554	        """Interpolate a 3-D field from model levels to CMIP6 plev19.
   555	
   556	        Parameters
   557	        ----------
   558	        field_3d : array, shape (..., nlev)
   559	            Field on model levels.
   560	        p_s : array, shape (...)
   561	            Surface pressure [Pa].
   562	
   563	        Returns (..., 19) numpy array on CMIP6 standard pressure levels,
   564	        or None if sigma_full is not available.
   565	        """
   566	        sigma = np.asarray(self.sigma_full)
   567	        p_s_np = np.asarray(p_s)
   568	        field_np = np.asarray(field_3d)
   569	
   570	        # Model pressure at each level: p_k = sigma_k * p_s
   571	        # Shape: (..., nlev)
   572	        p_model = p_s_np[..., None] * sigma
   573	
   574	        # Target pressure levels (ascending for interpolation)
   575	        plev_target = np.sort(CMIP6_PLEV19)  # ascending (100 Pa → 100000 Pa)
   576	
   577	        # Log-pressure linear interpolation (numpy version)
   578	        log_p_model = np.log(np.maximum(p_model, 1e-10))
   579	        log_plev = np.log(plev_target)
   580	
   581	        # Vectorise over the target-pressure axis instead of looping
   582	        # ``n_target`` times.  Each target level only needed two
   583	        # bracketing model levels and a log-linear interp; we can do
   584	        # all target levels in a single ``take_along_axis`` by
   585	        # broadcasting the searchsorted indices to ``(..., n_target)``.
   586	        # Iter 11: 19 full-grid NumPy passes per 3-D field → 1 vectorised
   587	        # pass per field.
   588	        n_target = len(plev_target)
   589	
   590	        # target_sigma shape: (..., n_target).  ``sigma`` is the ascending
   591	        # 1-D array of model layer-mid sigmas; for each cell we want the
   592	        # model-level index whose sigma first exceeds the target.
   593	        target_sigma = (
   594	            plev_target.reshape((1,) * p_s_np.ndim + (n_target,))
   595	            / np.maximum(p_s_np[..., None], 1e-10)
   596	        )
   597	        idx_hi = np.searchsorted(sigma, target_sigma)
   598	        idx_hi = np.clip(idx_hi, 1, len(sigma) - 1)
   599	        idx_lo = idx_hi - 1
   600	
   601	        f_lo = np.take_along_axis(field_np, idx_lo, axis=-1)
   602	        f_hi = np.take_along_axis(field_np, idx_hi, axis=-1)
   603	        lp_lo = np.take_along_axis(log_p_model, idx_lo, axis=-1)
   604	        lp_hi = np.take_along_axis(log_p_model, idx_hi, axis=-1)

   148	def vertical_del4_T_tendency(T_3d: jax.Array, nu_vert4_T: float) -> jax.Array:
   149	    """Scale-selective vertical biharmonic damping of the grid-scale T mode.
   150	
   151	    Returns the tendency ``-nu · ∂⁴T/∂σ⁴`` (a discrete fourth-difference on the
   152	    level INDEX — so ``nu_vert4_T`` is a filter RATE [1/s], NOT a physical
   153	    hyperdiffusivity like the horizontal ``nu_del4`` [m⁴/s]).  It damps the 2Δσ
   154	    (Nyquist) vertical mode while leaving resolved vertical structure
   155	    essentially untouched — the vertical analogue of the dycore's horizontal
   156	    ``nu_del4`` biharmonic hyperdiffusion.
   157	
   158	    Implemented as del2∘del2 (Laplacian of the Laplacian).  Boundary treatment:
   159	    the INNER Laplacian is ``reflect``-padded (so a 2Δσ mode keeps its full
   160	    ``-4`` Laplacian at the top/bottom levels — where the #930 checkerboard is
   161	    worst, at the low-pressure top), while the OUTER Laplacian is ``edge``
   162	    (zero-gradient) padded (a no-flux boundary → the column-integrated tendency
   163	    is ZERO to machine precision for ANY profile, so the filter dissipates
   164	    grid-scale variance WITHOUT spurious column heating/cooling).  Discrete 2Δσ
   165	    ``(-1)^k`` response: ``-16·nu`` in the interior, ``-8·nu`` at the top/bottom
   166	    (½ the interior rate — a boundary no-flux constraint of any conservative
   167	    biharmonic; still strong).  An 8Δσ resolved wave sees ``≈-0.34·nu``
   168	    (≈47× weaker than 2Δσ), so the filter is grid-scale-selective.
   169	
   170	    Parameters
   171	    ----------
   172	    T_3d : jax.Array
   173	        Temperature, shape ``(..., nlev)``.
   174	    nu_vert4_T : float
   175	        Biharmonic filter rate [1/s].  ``0.0`` ⇒ exact zero tendency.
   176	
   177	    Returns
   178	    -------
   179	    jax.Array
   180	        Vertical-hyperdiffusion tendency of T, same shape as ``T_3d``.
   181	    """
   182	    pad_axes = ((0, 0),) * (T_3d.ndim - 1)
   183	    # Inner Laplacian: reflect BC keeps the FULL 2Δσ response at the boundary
   184	    # levels (a plain edge/no-flux inner BC halves it again and leaves a slowly
   185	    # decaying top boundary mode).
   186	    Tp = jnp.pad(T_3d, (*pad_axes, (1, 1)), mode="reflect")
   187	    lap = Tp[..., :-2] - 2.0 * Tp[..., 1:-1] + Tp[..., 2:]      # ∂²/∂σ²
   188	    # Outer Laplacian: edge (zero-gradient / no-flux) BC ⇒ Σ_k tendency = 0
   189	    # exactly (flux form), so the filter conserves column-integrated T.
   190	    lap_p = jnp.pad(lap, (*pad_axes, (1, 1)), mode="edge")
   191	    bih = lap_p[..., :-2] - 2.0 * lap_p[..., 1:-1] + lap_p[..., 2:]  # ∂⁴/∂σ⁴ (>0 at 2Δσ)
   192	    return -nu_vert4_T * bih

codex
The CFL conclusion needs one qualification: sigma-advection itself is safely resolved at the stated values, but Bechtold contains an explicit `dp/(g·dt)` mass-flux CFL cap, and GWD accelerations are computed as stress divergence over `rho·dz` before their tendency caps. Those are controlled rather than a demonstrated blow-up mechanism, but the claim that no relevant term scales with layer thickness is too broad.

   201	def config_to_dict(config) -> dict:
   202	    """Generic config -> JSON-safe dict codec.
   203	
   204	    Thin delegator to the canonical home ``legoesm.driver.config.config_to_dict``
   205	    (federation carve, Step 3): a single implementation, kept here as a back-compat
   206	    entry point for callers that import it from ``forcing.amip_config``. Deferred
   207	    import avoids a forcing<->driver module-init cycle.
   208	    """
   209	    from legoesm.driver.config import config_to_dict as _impl
   210	    return _impl(config)
   211	
   212	
   213	def config_from_dict(d: dict):
   214	    """Reconstruct a config from a dict written by :func:`config_to_dict`.
   215	
   216	    Thin delegator to the canonical ``legoesm.driver.config.config_from_dict``
   217	    (auto-detects ExperimentConfig vs legacy flat AMIPExperimentConfig). Deferred
   218	    import avoids a forcing<->driver module-init cycle.
   219	    """
   220	    from legoesm.driver.config import config_from_dict as _impl
   221	    return _impl(d)

   224	def save_config(config: AMIPExperimentConfig, path: Path) -> None:
   225	    """Save experiment config to JSON."""
   226	    with open(path, "w") as f:
   227	        json.dump(config_to_dict(config), f, indent=2)
   228	
   229	
   230	def load_config(path: Path) -> AMIPExperimentConfig:
   231	    """Load experiment config from JSON."""
   232	    with open(path) as f:
   233	        return config_from_dict(json.load(f))

   240	def save_checkpoint(
   241	    path: Path,
   242	    state,
   243	    q_v: jnp.ndarray,
   244	    step: int,
   245	    day: float,
   246	    config,
   247	    diag_accumulators: dict | None = None,
   248	    q_c: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
   249	    q_r: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
   250	    carry_aux: dict | None = None,
   251	) -> None:
   252	    """Save a checkpoint for restart.
   253	
   254	    Parameters
   255	    ----------
   256	    path : Path
   257	        Output file path (.npz).
   258	    state : HydrostaticState
   259	        Atmospheric state (NamedTuple with Field members).
   260	    q_v : jax.Array
   261	        Moisture field, shape (6, n, n, nlev).
   262	    step : int
   263	        Current time step number.
   264	    day : float
   265	        Current simulation day.
   266	    config : ExperimentConfig or AMIPExperimentConfig
   267	        Experiment configuration (saved alongside for reproducibility).
   268	    diag_accumulators : dict, optional
   269	        Any accumulated diagnostic arrays to preserve across restart.
   270	    q_c : jax.Array, optional
   271	        Cloud water field, shape (6, n, n, nlev).
   272	    q_r : jax.Array, optional
   273	        Rain water field, shape (6, n, n, nlev).
   274	    """
   275	    # Extract state arrays
   276	    arrays = {
   277	        "T": np.asarray(state.T.data),
   278	        "u": np.asarray(state.u.data),
   279	        "v": np.asarray(state.v.data),
   280	        "p_s": np.asarray(state.p_s.data),
   281	        "phis": np.asarray(state.phis.data),
   282	        "q_v": np.asarray(q_v),
   283	        "step": np.array(step),
   284	        "day": np.array(day),
   285	    }
   285	    }
   286	
   287	    # Save hydrometeor fields if provided
   288	    if q_c is not None:
   289	        arrays["q_c"] = np.asarray(q_c)
   290	    if q_r is not None:
   291	        arrays["q_r"] = np.asarray(q_r)
   292	
   293	    # Save config as JSON string inside npz
   294	    arrays["config_json"] = np.array(json.dumps(config_to_dict(config)))
   295	
   296	    # Save diagnostic accumulators if provided
   297	    if diag_accumulators:
   298	        for k, v in diag_accumulators.items():
   299	            arrays[f"diag_{k}"] = np.asarray(v)
   300	
   301	    # Save carry auxiliary fields (held radiation, target_moisture, etc.)
   302	    if carry_aux:
   303	        for k, v in carry_aux.items():
   304	            arrays[f"carry_{k}"] = np.asarray(v)
   305	
   306	    np.savez(str(path), **arrays)

     1	"""Tropopause-refined sigma: redistribute layers at FIXED level count.
     2	
     3	The uniform-in-sigma default spaces every layer ~33 hPa at 30 levels, so
     4	the tropical tropopause layer gets ~3 levels and the model forms no cold
     5	point (measured 2026-07-25: coldest tropical level at the ~26 hPa lid).
     6	Adding levels does not fix the distribution and destabilised the model
     7	(L40 blow-up at day 46, dt=60).  These pin the redistribution: identity at
     8	refine=1, more TTL resolution at refine>1, and — the load-bearing safety
     9	property — no thinning of the top layers, which is what killed L40.
    10	"""
    11	
    12	import numpy as np
    13	import pytest
    14	
    15	from legoesm.grids.vertical import (
    16	    create_sigma_coordinate,
    17	    tropopause_refined_sigma_half,
    18	)

    20	P_S = 985.0  # hPa, the campaign's typical surface pressure
    21	
    22	
    23	def _dp(half):
    24	    return np.diff(np.asarray(half)) * P_S

    27	class TestGridProperties:
    28	    def test_identity_at_refine_one(self):
    29	        """refine=1 must reproduce the uniform grid EXACTLY — the default
    30	        path stays byte-identical."""
    31	        got = tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=1.0)
    32	        np.testing.assert_allclose(got, np.linspace(0.01, 1.0, 31), atol=1e-12)
    33	
    34	    def test_monotone_and_endpoints_exact(self):
    35	        for n in (20, 30, 40):
    36	            h = tropopause_refined_sigma_half(n, refine=3.0)
    37	            assert h.shape == (n + 1,)
    38	            assert np.all(np.diff(h) > 0)
    39	            assert h[0] == 0.01 and h[-1] == 1.0
    40	
    41	    def test_refinement_adds_ttl_levels(self):
    42	        """The whole point: more levels between 70 and 200 hPa."""
    43	        uni = tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=1.0) * P_S
    44	        ref = tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=3.0) * P_S
    45	        n_uni = int(((uni >= 70) & (uni <= 200)).sum())
    46	        n_ref = int(((ref >= 70) & (ref <= 200)).sum())
    47	        assert n_ref > n_uni, (n_uni, n_ref)
    48	
    49	    def test_ttl_spacing_improves(self):
    50	        """Layer thickness AT the tropopause shrinks."""
    51	        for h, label in ((tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=1.0), "uni"),
    52	                         (tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=3.0), "ref")):
    53	            p = np.asarray(h) * P_S
    54	            mid = 0.5 * (p[1:] + p[:-1])
    55	            near = np.abs(mid - 120.0) < 60.0
    56	            thick = _dp(h)[near].mean()
    57	            if label == "uni":
    58	                uni_thick = thick
    59	            else:
    60	                assert thick < 0.75 * uni_thick, (uni_thick, thick)
    61	
    62	    def test_top_layers_not_thinned(self):
    63	        """SAFETY: L40 died at day 46 because thin TOP layers destabilise the
    64	        model.  Redistribution must THICKEN the top, never thin it."""
    65	        uni = _dp(tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=1.0))
    66	        ref = _dp(tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=3.0))
    67	        assert ref[0] >= uni[0], (uni[0], ref[0])
    68	
    69	    def test_boundary_layer_cost_is_bounded(self):
    70	        """The boundary layer PAYS for the tropopause — an accepted, measured
    71	        cost, not a free lunch: the lowest layer coarsens ~30% (33 -> 42 hPa
    72	        at 30 levels, refine=3).  Pinned so a future density change cannot
    73	        quietly make it worse (and nowhere near the 166 hPa a naive
    74	        log-spaced grid would give)."""
    75	        uni = _dp(tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=1.0))
    76	        ref = _dp(tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=3.0))
    77	        assert 1.0 < ref[-1] / uni[-1] < 1.35, (uni[-1], ref[-1])
    78	
    79	    def test_layers_come_from_the_mid_troposphere(self):
    80	        """Conservation of levels: the TTL gain is paid for by the
    81	        (over-resolved) mid-troposphere, not the ends."""
    82	        uni = tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=1.0) * P_S
    83	        ref = tropopause_refined_sigma_half(30, refine=3.0) * P_S
    84	        band = lambda p, lo, hi: int(((p >= lo) & (p <= hi)).sum())  # noqa: E731
    85	        assert band(ref, 400, 800) < band(uni, 400, 800)
    86	
    87	    def test_monotone_in_refine_strength(self):

   112	    def test_refined_coordinate_is_self_consistent(self):
   113	        """The derived Simmons-Burridge quantities must stay finite and

     1	"""#930: MPAS single-column 2Δσ vertical-checkerboard cure + loud floor.
     2	
     3	Root cause (proven by ``test_2dz_is_undamped_null_mode_without_filter``): the
     4	MPAS hydrostatic thermodynamic equation has NO vertical damping of the
     5	grid-scale 2Δσ (Nyquist) vertical mode in T.  Vertical advection is upwind but
     6	vanishes where the vertical mass flux is weak; ω is smoothed (its 2Δσ part is
     7	killed by the half→full average).  So a 2Δσ mode is a *null mode* of the
     8	resolved T-tendency — a resting column with a ``(-1)^k`` T perturbation
     9	produces EXACTLY zero tendency.  The adiabatic term κ·T·ω/p then amplifies it
    10	in subsidence (1/p explodes at the low-pressure top levels) with nothing to
    11	oppose it, until it rides the silent ``T_min=50 K`` floor and rectifies into a
    12	checkerboard (#915 autopsy: even levels pinned at 50 K, odd exploding to 8e8 K).
    13	
    14	Cure: ``nu_vert4_T`` — a scale-selective vertical biharmonic (∂⁴/∂σ⁴)
    15	hyperdiffusion of T (the vertical analogue of the horizontal ``nu_del4``).  It
    16	removes the 2Δσ null mode at its source while leaving resolved vertical
    17	structure ~untouched and conserving column-integrated T.  With the cure on, the
    18	``T_min=50 K`` floor never binds (asserted below); it stays only as a last-
    19	resort guard, no longer the silent masker — #915's daily ``T < 100`` bounds
    20	guard aborts on any activation.
    21	"""
    22	
    23	from __future__ import annotations
    24	
    25	import numpy as np
    26	import jax
    27	import jax.numpy as jnp
    28	import pytest
    29	
    30	from legoesm.grids.voronoi import create_voronoi_mesh
    31	from legoesm.grids.vertical import create_sigma_coordinate
    32	from legoesm.core.state import MPASHydrostaticState
    33	from legoesm.core.field import Field
    34	from legoesm.atmosphere.dynamics.gcm.primitive_eq_mpas import (
    35	    MPASPrimitiveEquationModel,
    36	    MPASPrimitiveEquationConfig,
    37	    mpas_hydrostatic_tendencies,
    38	    vertical_del4_T_tendency,
    39	)
    40	
    41	pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    42	    not jax.config.read("jax_enable_x64"),
    43	    reason="dycore science test needs float64 (run with JAX_ENABLE_X64=1)",
    44	)
    45	
    46	
    47	NLEV = 24
    48	
    49	
    50	def _mesh():
    51	    return create_voronoi_mesh(2, lloyd_iterations=5)
    52	
    53	
    54	def _resting_state(mesh, nlev, seed_2dz=0.0, T0=250.0):
    55	    """Resting (u=0) isothermal column + optional 2Δσ T perturbation."""
    56	    k = np.arange(nlev)
    57	    Tcol = T0 + seed_2dz * (-1.0) ** k
    58	    nC, nE = mesh.nCells, mesh.nEdges
    59	    return MPASHydrostaticState(
    60	        u=Field(data=jnp.zeros((nE, nlev)), name="u",
    61	                dims=("nEdges", "nlev"), units="m/s"),
    62	        T=Field(data=jnp.asarray(np.tile(Tcol, (nC, 1))), name="T",
    63	                dims=("nCells", "nlev"), units="K"),
    64	        p_s=Field(data=jnp.full((nC,), 1.0e5), name="p_s",
    65	                  dims=("nCells",), units="Pa"),
    66	        phis=Field(data=jnp.zeros((nC,)), name="phis",
    67	                   dims=("nCells",), units="m^2/s^2"),
    68	    )
    69	
    70	
    71	def _amp_2dz(T_col):
    72	    k = np.arange(T_col.shape[-1])
    73	    return float(np.abs((np.asarray(T_col) * (-1.0) ** k).mean()))
    74	
    75	
    76	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    77	# Root cause: the 2Δσ mode is an undamped null mode without the filter.
    78	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    79	
    80	def test_2dz_is_undamped_null_mode_without_filter():
    81	    """A resting column with a 2Δσ T perturbation has ZERO tendency (the mode
    82	    is a null mode of the resolved T-tendency); the filter damps it."""
    83	    mesh = _mesh()
    84	    coord = create_sigma_coordinate(NLEV, sigma_top=1e-3)
    85	    state = _resting_state(mesh, NLEV, seed_2dz=1.0)
    86	
    87	    cfg0 = MPASPrimitiveEquationConfig(
    88	        nu_vert4_T=0.0, nu_del2=0.0, nu_del4=0.0, K_h=0.0)
    89	    tend0 = mpas_hydrostatic_tendencies(state, mesh, coord, cfg0, dt=60.0)
    90	    # No vertical damping of the 2Δσ mode: dT/dt is machine-zero.
    91	    assert float(jnp.abs(tend0.dT_dt.data).max()) < 1e-10
    92	
    93	    nu = 2.0e-6
    94	    cfg1 = MPASPrimitiveEquationConfig(
    95	        nu_vert4_T=nu, nu_del2=0.0, nu_del4=0.0, K_h=0.0)
    96	    tend1 = mpas_hydrostatic_tendencies(state, mesh, coord, cfg1, dt=60.0)
    97	    dT = tend1.dT_dt.data[0]
    98	    # The filter now produces a nonzero tendency that OPPOSES the 2Δσ mode
    99	    # (negative projection onto (-1)^k), i.e. it damps it.
   100	    k = np.arange(NLEV)
   101	    proj = float((np.asarray(dT) * (-1.0) ** k).mean())
   102	    assert proj < 0.0
   103	    # Interior response is ≈ -16·nu·amplitude (edge levels slightly weaker).
   104	    assert proj == pytest.approx(-16.0 * nu, rel=0.15)
   105	
   106	
   107	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   108	# Cure property: the vertical del4 filter is grid-scale selective.
   109	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   110	
   111	def test_vertical_del4_is_scale_selective():
   112	    nlev = 32
   113	    k = np.arange(nlev)
   114	    nu = 1.0e-3
   115	
   116	    T2 = jnp.asarray((-1.0) ** k)                     # 2Δσ (Nyquist)
   117	    t2 = vertical_del4_T_tendency(T2, nu)
   118	    rate_2dz = float(jnp.abs(t2[nlev // 2] / T2[nlev // 2]))
   119	    assert rate_2dz == pytest.approx(16.0 * nu, rel=1e-6)  # interior -16·nu
   120	
   121	    T8 = jnp.asarray(np.cos(np.pi * k / 4))           # 8Δσ resolved wave
   122	    t8 = vertical_del4_T_tendency(T8, nu)
   123	    rate_8dz = float(jnp.abs(t8[8] / T8[8]))
   124	    # del4 damps the 2Δσ mode ≥40× faster than an 8Δσ wave.
   125	    assert rate_2dz / rate_8dz > 40.0
   126	
   127	    # A smooth (quadratic) profile is essentially untouched.
   128	    sig = np.linspace(0.02, 0.99, nlev)
   129	    Tsm = jnp.asarray(200.0 + 100.0 * sig + 50.0 * sig ** 2)
   130	    tsm = vertical_del4_T_tendency(Tsm, nu)
   131	    smooth_rate = float(jnp.abs(tsm).max() / Tsm.max())
   132	    assert smooth_rate < rate_2dz / 100.0
   133	
   134	    # nu == 0 is exactly zero (bit-identical pre-fix path) — even for an
   135	    # arbitrary (random) profile, so nu_vert4_T=0 is a true no-op.
   136	    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
   137	    Trand = jnp.asarray(rng.randn(nlev) * 40.0 + 250.0)
   138	    assert float(jnp.abs(vertical_del4_T_tendency(Trand, 0.0)).max()) == 0.0
   139	
   140	
   141	def test_vertical_del4_boundary_damped_and_column_conservative():
   142	    """The top/bottom boundary levels (where the #930 blowup is worst) are
   143	    damped at ½ the interior rate — a no-flux boundary constraint of any
   144	    conservative biharmonic — and the operator conserves column-integrated T
   145	    to machine precision for ANY profile (flux form, not accidental)."""
   146	    nlev = 32
   147	    k = np.arange(nlev)
   148	    nu = 1.0e-3
   149	    T2 = jnp.asarray((-1.0) ** k)
   150	    t2 = vertical_del4_T_tendency(T2, nu)
   151	    # Boundary 2Δσ response is -8·nu (½ the interior -16·nu) — reduced but
   152	    # strong, and NOT in the null space (would be 0 without the reflect inner BC).
   153	    assert float(jnp.abs(t2[0] / T2[0])) == pytest.approx(8.0 * nu, rel=1e-6)
   154	    assert float(jnp.abs(t2[-1] / T2[-1])) == pytest.approx(8.0 * nu, rel=1e-6)
   155	
   156	    # Column-integrated-T conservation for arbitrary profiles (even + odd nlev,
   157	    # random amplitudes) — refutes the "only accidental for symmetric fields"
   158	    # concern: the outer edge (no-flux) Laplacian makes Σ_k tendency ≡ 0.
   159	    rng = np.random.RandomState(3)
   160	    for n in (24, 31, 17):
   161	        Tr = jnp.asarray(rng.randn(n) * 40.0 + 250.0)
   162	        col_sum = float(jnp.sum(vertical_del4_T_tendency(Tr, nu)))
   163	        scale = float(jnp.abs(vertical_del4_T_tendency(Tr, nu)).max())
   164	        assert abs(col_sum) < 1e-10 * max(scale, 1.0)
   165	
   166	
   167	def test_vertical_del4_is_differentiable():
   168	    """AD-safe: the cure helper has a finite gradient (end-to-end grad goal)."""
   169	    k = np.arange(NLEV)
   170	    T = jnp.asarray(250.0 + (-1.0) ** k)
   171	    g = jax.grad(lambda x: jnp.sum(vertical_del4_T_tendency(x, 2e-6) ** 2))(T)
   172	    assert bool(jnp.all(jnp.isfinite(g)))
   173	
   174	
   175	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   176	# Integration: the real dycore step preserves the 2Δσ mode without the cure
   177	# (undamped null mode) and decays it with the cure — and the floor never fires.
   178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179	
   180	def test_real_step_damps_2dz_and_floor_stays_dead():
   181	    mesh = _mesh()
   182	    coord = create_sigma_coordinate(NLEV, sigma_top=1e-3)
   183	    nsteps = 50
   184	    seed = 2.0
   185	
   186	    def integrate(nu):
   187	        state = _resting_state(mesh, NLEV, seed_2dz=seed)
   188	        model = MPASPrimitiveEquationModel(
   189	            mesh=mesh, sigma_coord=coord,
   190	            config=MPASPrimitiveEquationConfig(
   191	                nu_vert4_T=nu, nu_del2=0.0, nu_del4=0.0, K_h=0.0,
   192	                fix_mass=True),
   193	        )
   194	        a0 = _amp_2dz(state.T.data[0])
   195	        tmin_hist = []
   196	        for _ in range(nsteps):
   197	            state = model.step(state, dt=60.0)
   198	            tmin_hist.append(float(state.T.data.min()))
   199	        return a0, _amp_2dz(state.T.data[0]), min(tmin_hist), state
   200	
   201	    a0_off, a_off, tmin_off, _ = integrate(0.0)
   202	    a0_on, a_on, tmin_on, st_on = integrate(2.0e-4)
   203	
   204	    # Without the cure: 2Δσ mode is a null mode — preserved (undamped).
   205	    assert a_off / a0_off > 0.99
   206	    # With the cure: strongly damped.
   207	    assert a_on / a0_on < 0.1
   208	    # The T_min=50 K floor never fires in either resting-column run
   209	    # (no clamp activations — Tmin stays far above 50 K).
   210	    assert tmin_off > 100.0 and tmin_on > 100.0
   211	    assert bool(jnp.all(jnp.isfinite(st_on.T.data)))
   212

   215	# Regression guards on the config defaults (off in the dycore, on in production).
   216	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   217	
   218	def test_config_defaults():
   219	    # Base dycore config: off by default => pre-#930 bit-identical.
   220	    assert MPASPrimitiveEquationConfig().nu_vert4_T == 0.0
   221	    # Production (coupled/AMIP) default: the cure is on.
   222	    from legoesm.driver.config import DycoreConfig
   223	    assert DycoreConfig().mpas_nu_vert4_T > 0.0

   161	    the INNER Laplacian is ``reflect``-padded (so a 2Δσ mode keeps its full

   163	    worst, at the low-pressure top), while the OUTER Laplacian is ``edge``
   164	    (zero-gradient) padded (a no-flux boundary → the INDEX-space sum
   165	    ``Σ_k tendency_k`` is ZERO to machine precision for ANY profile).

   167	    MASS-weighted ``Σ_k tendency_k · Δσ_k``, and the two coincide only when

+    point (its coldest tropical level lands at the ~26 hPa top instead of
+    ~100 hPa; measured 2026-07-25).  Adding levels does NOT fix this: at

   125	        :func:`tropopause_refined_sigma_half`).  ``1.0`` (default) is the

   140	    # with float32 state arrays triggers scatter-cast warnings).

   194	
   195	    The uniform-in-sigma default (:func:`create_sigma_coordinate`) spaces
   196	    every layer by the same ``dp = dsigma * p_s`` — about 33 hPa at 30
   197	    levels — so the tropical tropopause layer, whose structure is a
   198	    10-20 hPa affair, is spanned by ~3 levels and the model forms no cold
   199	    point (its coldest tropical level lands at the ~26 hPa top instead of
   200	    ~100 hPa; measured 2026-07-25).  Adding levels does NOT fix this: at
   201	    40 levels the TTL still gets 4 levels, and that L40 run (uniform σ,
   202	    24.4 hPa in EVERY layer) blew up at day 46 with dt=60.  The L40 failure
   203	    mode is NOT attributed here — it appeared across levels 0-11 (10-302 hPa)
   204	    and no mechanism has been instrumented; "thin layers destabilise" is an
   205	    untested hypothesis, so it is not used as a design argument below.
   206	
   207	    So redistribute at FIXED count instead.  Levels are placed by the
   208	    standard equidistribution principle: they are the quantiles of a
   209	    density ``d(sigma)`` in SIGMA space, so a flat density reproduces the
   210	    uniform default exactly and the refinement only steals layers from the
   211	    (over-resolved) mid-troposphere::
   212	
   213	        d(sigma) = 1 + (refine - 1) * exp(-0.5 * ((ln sigma - ln sigma_refine) / width)^2)
   214	
   215	    The bump is Gaussian in LOG sigma because atmospheric structure scales
   216	    with log-pressure; ``width`` is therefore in log-sigma units (0.45 ~ a
   217	    factor e^0.45 = 1.6 in pressure either side of the centre).  Working in
   218	    sigma (not log-sigma) for the equidistribution is deliberate: a pure
   219	    log-sigma grid would put 166 hPa between the lowest levels at 30
   220	    levels and destroy the boundary layer.
   221	
   222	    Parameters
   223	    ----------
   224	    n_levels : int
   225	        Number of layers (returns ``n_levels + 1`` half levels).
   226	    sigma_top : float

   228	        :func:`create_sigma_coordinate`).
   229	    sigma_refine : float
   230	        Centre of the refinement, in sigma (0.12 ~ 120 hPa at p_s = 1000
   231	        hPa — the tropical cold point).
   232	    refine : float
   233	        Peak density ratio.  ``refine = 1`` reproduces the uniform grid
   234	        EXACTLY (the identity case, pinned by a test).
   235	    width : float
   236	        Gaussian half-width of the bump in log-sigma units.
   237	
   238	    Returns

   255	    s = np.linspace(sigma_top, 1.0, 20001, dtype=np.float64)

   261	    # the lowest layer (42 -> 23 hPa) but it is very WIDE in sigma (it spans
   262	    # sigma ~ 0.6-1.0), so it starves the tropopause back to 5 levels from 8
   263	    # and thickens the TOP layer to 57 hPa.  At 30 levels the grid cannot
   264	    # refine both ends; the tropopause is the identified defect, so it wins.
   265	    # ACCEPTED COSTS, both measured at nlev=30 / refine=3, both real:
   266	    #   (a) the lowest layer coarsens ~30% (33 -> 42 hPa);
   267	    #   (b) the thinnest layer is 14.2 hPa at ~113 hPa — 42% THINNER than
   268	    #       anything the L40 run that blew up ever had, and inside the same
   269	    #       10-302 hPa band where that failure appeared.  The top layer k=0
   270	    #       does thicken (33 -> 40 hPa), but that covers ONE level of a
   271	    #       twelve-level failure, so it is NOT a safety argument.
   272	    #   (c) the max adjacent-layer thickness ratio rises 1.00 -> 1.62,
   273	    #       vs <= 1.07 on every grid this model has run successfully.

   275	    # density, so spacing ~ 1/d — fine where d is large.
   276	    cum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(0.5 * (dens[1:] + dens[:-1])

   283	    # p_s = sigma=1 identity both assume).
   284	    half[0], half[-1] = sigma_top, 1.0

"""Diagnostic collection for the composable model driver.

Extracts the diagnostic accumulation, snapshot capture, and output
logic from run_amip.py into a reusable class.
"""

class _StructuredRegridWeights:
    """Precomputed bilinear interpolation weights for structured grids."""
    __slots__ = ('i_lo', 'j_lo', 'wi', 'wj', 'src_nlat', 'src_nlon')

    def __init__(self, i_lo, j_lo, wi, wj, src_nlat, src_nlon):
        self.i_lo = i_lo
        self.j_lo = j_lo
        self.wi = wi
        self.wj = wj
        self.src_nlat = src_nlat
        self.src_nlon = src_nlon


def _build_structured_regrid_weights(
    src_lat_rad: np.ndarray,
    src_lon_rad: np.ndarray,
    tgt_nlat: int,
    tgt_nlon: int,
) -> _StructuredRegridWeights:
    """Build bilinear interpolation weights from a native structured grid
    to a regular CMIP lat-lon grid.

    Parameters
    ----------
    src_lat_rad : (n_lat_src,) — source latitudes in radians, S→N
    src_lon_rad : (n_lon_src,) — source longitudes in radians, [0, 2π)
    tgt_nlat, tgt_nlon : target CMIP grid dimensions
    """
    src_lat = np.degrees(src_lat_rad)  # S→N
    src_lon = np.degrees(src_lon_rad)  # [0, 360)

    dlat = 180.0 / tgt_nlat
    dlon = 360.0 / tgt_nlon
    tgt_lat = np.linspace(-90.0 + dlat / 2, 90.0 - dlat / 2, tgt_nlat)
    tgt_lon = np.linspace(dlon / 2, 360.0 - dlon / 2, tgt_nlon)

    # For each target lat, find bracketing source lat indices + weight
    i_lo = np.searchsorted(src_lat, tgt_lat) - 1
    i_lo = np.clip(i_lo, 0, len(src_lat) - 2)
    denom_i = src_lat[i_lo + 1] - src_lat[i_lo]
    denom_i = np.where(denom_i == 0, 1.0, denom_i)
    wi = np.clip((tgt_lat - src_lat[i_lo]) / denom_i, 0.0, 1.0)

    # For each target lon, find bracketing source lon indices + weight
    j_lo = np.searchsorted(src_lon, tgt_lon) - 1
    j_lo = np.clip(j_lo, 0, len(src_lon) - 2)
    denom_j = src_lon[j_lo + 1] - src_lon[j_lo]
    denom_j = np.where(denom_j == 0, 1.0, denom_j)
    wj = np.clip((tgt_lon - src_lon[j_lo]) / denom_j, 0.0, 1.0)

    return _StructuredRegridWeights(
        i_lo=i_lo, j_lo=j_lo, wi=wi, wj=wj,
        src_nlat=len(src_lat), src_nlon=len(src_lon),
    )


def _apply_structured_regrid_2d(
    field: np.ndarray,
    w: _StructuredRegridWeights,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Apply bilinear interpolation to a 2-D field (nlat_src, nlon_src)
    → (nlat_tgt, nlon_tgt)."""
    i0 = w.i_lo
    i1 = np.minimum(i0 + 1, w.src_nlat - 1)
    j0 = w.j_lo
    j1 = np.minimum(j0 + 1, w.src_nlon - 1)
    wi = w.wi
    wj = w.wj
    # Bilinear: f = (1-wi)(1-wj)*f00 + wi*(1-wj)*f10 + (1-wi)*wj*f01 + wi*wj*f11
    f00 = field[np.ix_(i0, j0)]
    f10 = field[np.ix_(i1, j0)]
    f01 = field[np.ix_(i0, j1)]
    f11 = field[np.ix_(i1, j1)]
    return ((1 - wi[:, None]) * (1 - wj[None, :]) * f00
            + wi[:, None] * (1 - wj[None, :]) * f10
            + (1 - wi[:, None]) * wj[None, :] * f01
            + wi[:, None] * wj[None, :] * f11)


def _apply_structured_regrid_3d(
    field: np.ndarray,
    w: _StructuredRegridWeights,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Apply bilinear interpolation to a 3-D field (nlat_src, nlon_src, nlev)
    → (nlat_tgt, nlon_tgt, nlev).

    neighbours once and apply the per-cell weights with NumPy
    broadcasting instead of looping ``nlev`` times.  At T63L49 with
    ~50 levels this turns 50 separate per-level NumPy calls into one.
    """

    i1 = np.minimum(i0 + 1, w.src_nlat - 1)
    j0 = w.j_lo

    35	def area_weighted_mean(field: jax.Array, area: jax.Array | None) -> jax.Array:
    36	    """Area-weighted global mean of a horizontal (optionally layered) field.
    37	
    38	    ``jnp.mean`` weights every grid cell equally.  On a lat-lon grid the
    39	    polar rows then count as much as the equatorial rows despite each cell
    40	    spanning ``~cos(lat)`` less area, biasing every global-mean diagnostic
    41	    toward the cold, ice-covered high latitudes.  On a 24-band coupled run
    42	    this pulled ``<rsdt>`` to ~281 W/m² (the true area-weighted value is the
    43	    energy-conserving ``S_0/4`` = 340 W/m²) and manufactured a ``<R_TOA>`` ≈
    44	    −36 W/m² "cold drift" where the area-weighted TOA budget is near balance.
    45	    Weight each cell by its true area instead.
    46	
    47	    Parameters
    48	    ----------
    49	    field : array
    50	        Field whose leading axes are the horizontal grid (shape matching
    51	        ``area``).  Any trailing axes (e.g. vertical levels) are averaged
    52	        uniformly first, reproducing ``jnp.mean`` semantics in those axes.
    53	    area : array or None
    54	        Per-cell area with the field's horizontal shape (``grid.grid_area``;
    55	        lat-lon ``(n_lat, n_lon)``, cube ``(6, n, n)``).  Need not be
    56	        normalized.  ``None`` falls back to an unweighted ``jnp.mean`` — cube
    57	        cells are ~equal area, and legacy callers / tests stay byte-identical.
    58	    """
    59	    if area is None:
    60	        return jnp.mean(field)
    61	    nh = area.ndim
    62	    # Defensive: a field whose horizontal axes don't match ``area`` (e.g. an
    63	    # ocean field on a different grid than the atmosphere's area) falls back
    64	    # to an unweighted mean rather than broadcasting silently.
    65	    if field.ndim < nh or tuple(field.shape[:nh]) != tuple(area.shape):
    66	        return jnp.mean(field)
    67	    if field.ndim > nh:
    68	        field = jnp.mean(field, axis=tuple(range(nh, field.ndim)))
    69	    return jnp.sum(field * area) / jnp.sum(area)
    70	
    71	
    72	def area_weighted_profile(field: jax.Array, area: jax.Array | None) -> jax.Array:
    73	    """Area-weighted horizontal mean retaining the trailing (vertical) axis.
    74	
    75	    Companion to :func:`area_weighted_mean` for level-resolved profiles.
    76	    ``field`` has horizontal leading axes matching ``area`` plus one trailing
    77	    level axis; returns the area-weighted mean over the horizontal axes only,
    78	    shape ``(nlev,)``.  ``area=None`` falls back to an unweighted horizontal
    79	    mean (``jnp.mean`` over all-but-last axis).
    80	    """
    81	    spatial_axes = tuple(range(field.ndim - 1))
    82	    if area is None:
    83	        return jnp.mean(field, axis=spatial_axes)
    84	    nh = area.ndim
    85	    # Same defensive guard as ``area_weighted_mean``: a field whose horizontal
    86	    # axes don't match ``area`` (wrong grid, or no trailing level axis) falls
    87	    # back to a plain horizontal mean rather than broadcasting silently.
    88	    if field.ndim <= nh or tuple(field.shape[:nh]) != tuple(area.shape):
    89	        return jnp.mean(field, axis=spatial_axes)
    90	    w = area[..., None]
    91	    return jnp.sum(field * w, axis=spatial_axes) / jnp.sum(area)

    71	def column_mass_weighted_mean(field, mass_per_cell, axis: int = -1):
    72	    """FV3_3D iter 605: column mass-weighted mean of a 3D field.
    73	
    74	    Faithful port of FV3 ``dyn_core.F90:1313-1326`` (the d_ext
    75	    external-mode-damping column-mean computation):
    76	
    77	        out(i,j) = Σ_k mass[k] · field[k] / Σ_k mass[k]
    78	
    79	    Used by FV3's d_ext > 0 external (barotropic) mode damping
    80	    branch where ``field = vt`` (divergence-flux) and ``mass =
    81	    ptc[k]`` (column mass weight per level).  Also useful for
    82	    other column diagnostics (e.g., mass-weighted-mean potential
    83	    temperature, mass-weighted divergence).
    84	
    85	    Parameters
    86	    ----------
    87	    field : jax.Array, shape (..., nlev)
    88	        Field to average.
    89	    mass_per_cell : jax.Array, shape (..., nlev)
    90	        Mass weight per level (delp, rho·dz, etc.).
    91	    axis : int, default -1
    92	        Vertical axis.
    93	
    94	    Returns
    95	    -------
    96	    jax.Array, same shape as field minus the vertical axis.
    97	        Column mass-weighted mean.
    98	
    99	    Notes
   100	    -----
   101	    Guards against zero total mass (returns 0 in that case).
   102	    """
   103	    weighted_sum = jnp.sum(field * mass_per_cell, axis=axis)
   104	    total_mass = jnp.sum(mass_per_cell, axis=axis)
   105	    return jnp.where(
   106	        jnp.abs(total_mass) > 1e-30,
   107	        weighted_sum / jnp.where(jnp.abs(total_mass) > 1e-30,
   108	                                  total_mass, 1.0),
   109	        0.0,
   110	    )

   543	# ======================================================================
   544	# Moisture Budget Tracker
   545	# ======================================================================
   546	
   547	class MoistureBudget(NamedTuple):
   548	    """Snapshot of moisture budget diagnostics (global means)."""
   549	    column_water: float      # column-integrated water vapor [kg/m²]
   550	    dW_dt: float             # water vapor tendency [kg/m²/s]
   551	    precip_rate: float       # precipitation rate [mm/day]
   552	    evap_rate: float         # surface evaporation rate [mm/day]
   553	    residual: float          # E − P − dW/dt [mm/day] (0 = closed column)
   554	
   555	
   556	class MoistureBudgetTracker:
   557	    """Track moisture budget evolution over a simulation.
   558	
   559	    Tracks column-integrated water vapor and its tendency, precipitation,
   560	    surface evaporation, and the moisture budget CLOSURE residual
   561	    E − P − dW/dt.  For a well-conserving model, the annual-mean residual
   562	    should be < 0.01 mm/day.
   563	
   564	    Sign convention: E (evaporation, from the latent heat flux) is
   565	    positive UPWARD = a vapor source for the atmospheric column; P
   566	    (surface precipitation) is positive = a column sink; dW/dt is the
   567	    column vapor storage tendency.  A closed column satisfies
   568	    E − P − dW/dt = 0.  (The pre-2026-07-22 residual was dW/dt + P — the
   569	    net apparent source — which never ingested E and equals ~P in steady
   570	    state, so it could NOT detect a vapor-destroying process; the 2-yr
   571	    AMIP pilot's 1.4 mm/day E−P non-closure sailed through it.)
   572	
   573	    Usage
   574	    -----
   575	    tracker = MoistureBudgetTracker()
   576	    tracker.update(q_v, p_s, dsigma, precip, lhflx, elapsed_seconds)
   577	    print(tracker.summary())
   578	    """
   579	
   580	    def __init__(self):
   581	        self.times: list[float] = []
   582	        self.column_water: list[float] = []
   583	        self.precip_rate: list[float] = []
   584	        self.evap_rate: list[float] = []
   585	        self.dW_dt: list[float] = []
   586	        self.residual: list[float] = []
   587	        self._prev_water: float | None = None
   588	        self._prev_time: float | None = None
   589	
   590	    def update(
   591	        self,
   592	        q_v: jax.Array,
   593	        p_s: jax.Array,
   594	        dsigma: jax.Array,
   595	        precip: jax.Array,
   596	        lhflx: jax.Array,
   597	        elapsed_seconds: float,
   598	        area_weights: jax.Array | None = None,
   599	    ) -> MoistureBudget:
   600	        """Compute and record moisture budget at current time.
   601	
   602	        Parameters
   603	        ----------
   604	        q_v : array, shape (..., nlev)
   605	            Specific humidity [kg/kg].
   606	        p_s : array, shape (...)
   607	            Surface pressure [Pa].
   608	        dsigma : array, shape (nlev,)
   609	            Sigma layer thicknesses.
   610	        precip : array, shape (...)
   611	            Precipitation rate [kg/m²/s], positive = column sink.
   612	        lhflx : array, shape (...)
   613	            Surface latent heat flux [W/m²], positive upward — converted
   614	            to the evaporation vapor source E = lhflx / L_v.  Pass the
   615	            SAME field reported as CMOR ``hfls`` so the closure check and
   616	            the output diagnostics share one flux definition.
   617	        elapsed_seconds : float
   618	            Time since simulation start [s].
   619	
   620	        Returns
   621	        -------
   622	        MoistureBudget
   623	        """
   624	        W = column_water_vapor(q_v, p_s, dsigma)
   625	        # Fuse the column-water-vapor + precip + evap means into one
   626	        # host transfer.
   627	        _h = np.asarray(jnp.stack([
   628	            area_weighted_mean(W, area_weights),
   629	            area_weighted_mean(precip, area_weights),
   630	            area_weighted_mean(lhflx, area_weights),
   631	        ]))
   632	        mean_W = float(_h[0])
   633	        mean_P = float(_h[1]) * 86400.0                  # kg/m²/s → mm/day
   634	        mean_E = float(_h[2]) / constants.L_v * 86400.0  # W/m² → mm/day
   635	
   636	        # Tendency
   637	        if self._prev_water is not None and self._prev_time is not None:
   638	            dt = elapsed_seconds - self._prev_time
   639	            if dt > 0:
   640	                dW_dt = (mean_W - self._prev_water) / dt
   641	            else:
   642	                dW_dt = 0.0
   643	            # CLOSURE residual: E − P − dW/dt = 0 for a conserving column
   644	            # (E positive-up source, P positive sink — see class docstring).
   645	            # A POSITIVE residual = water destroyed inside the atmosphere
   646	            # (vapor entered via E but reached neither storage nor precip);
   647	            # negative = spurious source.  The 2-yr AMIP pilot's signature
   648	            # is residual ≈ +1.4 mm/day.
   649	            residual_mm_day = mean_E - mean_P - dW_dt * 86400.0
   650	        else:
   651	            dW_dt = 0.0
   652	            residual_mm_day = 0.0
   653	
   654	        self._prev_water = mean_W
   655	        self._prev_time = elapsed_seconds
   656	
   657	        budget = MoistureBudget(
   658	            column_water=mean_W,
   659	            dW_dt=dW_dt,
   660	            precip_rate=mean_P,
   661	            evap_rate=mean_E,
   662	            residual=residual_mm_day,
   663	        )
   664	
   665	        self.times.append(elapsed_seconds)
   666	        self.column_water.append(mean_W)
   667	        self.precip_rate.append(mean_P)
   668	        self.evap_rate.append(mean_E)
   669	        self.dW_dt.append(dW_dt)
   670	        self.residual.append(residual_mm_day)
   671	
   672	        return budget
   673	
   674	    def flush_to_lists(self) -> dict[str, list]:
   675	        """Return and clear accumulated lists (for periodic flush)."""
   676	        data = {
   677	            "times": self.times,
   678	            "column_water": self.column_water,
   679	            "precip_rate": self.precip_rate,
   680	            "evap_rate": self.evap_rate,
   681	            "dW_dt": self.dW_dt,
   682	            "residual": self.residual,
   683	        }
   684	        self.times = []
   685	        self.column_water = []
   686	        self.precip_rate = []
   687	        self.evap_rate = []
   688	        self.dW_dt = []
   689	        self.residual = []
   690	        return data

+def tropopause_refined_sigma_half(
+    n_levels: int,
+    sigma_top: float = 0.01,
+    sigma_refine: float = 0.12,
+    refine: float = 3.0,
+    width: float = 0.45,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Half-level sigma with layers REDISTRIBUTED toward the tropopause.
+
+    The uniform-in-sigma default (:func:`create_sigma_coordinate`) spaces
+    every layer by the same ``dp = dsigma * p_s`` — about 33 hPa at 30
+    levels — so the tropical tropopause layer, whose structure is a
+    10-20 hPa affair, is spanned by ~3 levels and the model forms no cold
+    point (its coldest tropical level lands at the ~26 hPa top instead of
+    ~100 hPa; measured 2026-07-25).  Adding levels does NOT fix this: at
+    40 levels the TTL still gets 4 levels, and that L40 run (uniform σ,
+    24.4 hPa in EVERY layer) blew up at day 46 with dt=60.  The L40 failure
+    mode is NOT attributed here — it appeared across levels 0-11 (10-302 hPa)
+    and no mechanism has been instrumented; "thin layers destabilise" is an
+    untested hypothesis, so it is not used as a design argument below.
+
+    So redistribute at FIXED count instead.  Levels are placed by the
+    standard equidistribution principle: they are the quantiles of a
+    density ``d(sigma)`` in SIGMA space, so a flat density reproduces the
+    uniform default exactly and the refinement only steals layers from the
+    (over-resolved) mid-troposphere::
+
+        d(sigma) = 1 + (refine - 1) * exp(-0.5 * ((ln sigma - ln sigma_refine) / width)^2)
+
+    The bump is Gaussian in LOG sigma because atmospheric structure scales
+    with log-pressure; ``width`` is therefore in log-sigma units (0.45 ~ a
+    factor e^0.45 = 1.6 in pressure either side of the centre).  Working in
+    sigma (not log-sigma) for the equidistribution is deliberate: a pure
+    log-sigma grid would put 166 hPa between the lowest levels at 30
+    levels and destroy the boundary layer.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    n_levels : int
+        Number of layers (returns ``n_levels + 1`` half levels).
+    sigma_top : float
+        Sigma of the model top (same meaning as in
+        :func:`create_sigma_coordinate`).
+    sigma_refine : float
+        Centre of the refinement, in sigma (0.12 ~ 120 hPa at p_s = 1000
+        hPa — the tropical cold point).
+    refine : float
+        Peak density ratio.  ``refine = 1`` reproduces the uniform grid
+        EXACTLY (the identity case, pinned by a test).
+    width : float
+        Gaussian half-width of the bump in log-sigma units.
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    numpy.ndarray, shape ``(n_levels + 1,)``
+        Monotone increasing half-level sigma from ``sigma_top`` to 1.
+    """
+    if not (refine >= 1.0 and width > 0.0):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"tropopause_refined_sigma_half: need refine >= 1 and width > 0; "
+            f"got refine={refine!r}, width={width!r}")
+    if not (0.0 < sigma_top < sigma_refine < 1.0):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"tropopause_refined_sigma_half: need 0 < sigma_top < "
+            f"sigma_refine < 1; got sigma_top={sigma_top!r}, "
+            f"sigma_refine={sigma_refine!r}")
+    # Fine auxiliary QUADRATURE grid; the quantile inversion below is a 1-D
+    # interp, so resolution here only sets the placement accuracy (not a
+    # runtime cost: this runs once at setup, on the host, in float64).
+    # LOG-spaced, matching the density's own log-σ structure: a σ-uniform mesh
+    # has constant Δσ ≈ 5e-5 and therefore CANNOT resolve a narrow bump placed
+    # near the lid (``width`` 0.02 at ``sigma_refine`` ≈ ``sigma_top`` = 1e-5
+    # spans Δσ ~ 2e-7, i.e. zero mesh points), giving a worst-case placement
+    # error of 3.1e-5 in σ over the allowed parameter box.  The log mesh
+    # resolves every allowed bump uniformly: worst case 2.0e-7 (155x better),
+    # and it moves the DEFAULT grid by only 7.8e-9 in σ (8e-6 hPa) — toward
+    # the exact answer, not away.  ``refine == 1`` stays exact either way
+    # (a constant integrand is exact under the trapezoid on any mesh).
+    s = np.geomspace(sigma_top, 1.0, 20001, dtype=np.float64)
+    _ln = np.log(s)
+    dens = 1.0 + (refine - 1.0) * np.exp(
+        -0.5 * ((_ln - np.log(sigma_refine)) / width) ** 2)
+    # DELIBERATELY single-bump.  A matching surface bump was tried and
+    # rejected (measured 2026-07-25, 30 levels, refine=3): it does protect
+    # the lowest layer (42 -> 23 hPa) but it is very WIDE in sigma (it spans
+    # sigma ~ 0.6-1.0), so it starves the tropopause back to 5 levels from 8
+    # and thickens the TOP layer to 57 hPa.  At 30 levels the grid cannot
+    # refine both ends; the tropopause is the identified defect, so it wins.
+    # ACCEPTED COSTS, both measured at nlev=30 / refine=3, both real:
+    #   (a) the lowest layer coarsens ~30% (33 -> 42 hPa);
+    #   (b) the thinnest layer is 14.2 hPa at ~113 hPa — 42% THINNER than
+    #       anything the L40 run that blew up ever had, and inside the same
+    #       10-302 hPa band where that failure appeared.  The top layer k=0
+    #       does thicken (33 -> 40 hPa), but that covers ONE level of a
+    #       twelve-level failure, so it is NOT a safety argument.
+    #   (c) the max adjacent-layer thickness ratio rises 1.00 -> 1.62,
+    #       vs <= 1.07 on every grid this model has run successfully.

+    # p_s = sigma=1 identity both assume).
+    half[0], half[-1] = sigma_top, 1.0

Verdict: not ready for production. The current worktree fixes parts of F1/F2/F3 while I reviewed it, but has remaining correctness blockers.

- The new del4 “conservation” fix is wrong for hybrid coordinates. It passes `sigma_coord.dsigma`, which for hybrid is only `dA + dB`, not physical layer mass. Physical weights are `dp = p_ref*dA + p_s*dB`, column-dependent. Thus it still does not conserve hybrid column water/enthalpy except at `p_s=p_ref`. [primitive_eq_mpas.py:573](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/dynamics/gcm/primitive_eq_mpas.py:573), [vertical.py:728](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:728), [vertical.py:998](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:998)

  Mean removal is the right immediate compatibility fix for pure sigma: subtract the weighted mean using `dsigma` (or `dp`, whose column factor cancels). For hybrid, pass `layer_thickness_dp(p_s)`. A metric-aware flux-form del4 is the better long-term operator, but should be a separately tuned/versioned operator: it changes scale-selective damping relative to the index-rate filter.

- Restart protection is incomplete. The new MPAS `meta_sigma_half` catches normal uniform-L30 versus refine-3-L30 restarts written by the new code, but:
  - pre-guard checkpoints silently bypass it;
  - `atol=1e-6` permits genuine small coordinate changes;
  - hybrid `sigma_half` is only `A+B`, so it does not fingerprint the actual `A/B` pressure mapping;
  - non-MPAS restart paths remain unguarded: `load_restart` returns the saved config, then `ModelDriver` discards it. [model_driver.py:4875](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/model_driver.py:4875), [model_driver.py:5313](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/model_driver.py:5313), [restart.py:841](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/restart.py:841)

  Store and exactly compare a coordinate fingerprint: coordinate type plus sigma interfaces for sigma, and `A_half`, `B_half`, and `p_ref` for hybrid. Legacy files should require an explicit unsafe override, not silently proceed.

- `--p-top` remains silently ignored on sigma runs. The sigma branch only passes `nlev` and refinement, so it always uses `sigma_top=0.01`; at 985 hPa this is a 9.85 hPa lid, not the configured default `p_top_Pa=200` Pa. [model_driver.py:996](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/model_driver.py:996), [run_amip.py:1584](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/run/run_amip.py:1584) This is pre-existing, but the new sigma feature makes it operationally important. Expose `sigma_top`, or reject non-default `p_top_Pa` on sigma; a fixed-pressure top is not generally compatible with pure sigma.

- The public quadrature API accepts unresolved bumps. It only requires `width > 0`, while using a fixed 20,001-point log mesh. [vertical.py:243](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:243), [vertical.py:252](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:252) For `width=1e-6` and `sigma_refine` halfway between two log-mesh nodes, every sampled Gaussian contribution underflows and `refine=6` produces an effectively flat grid. It also accepts `refine=inf`, `width=inf`, and `n_levels=0`.

  The current switch from `linspace` to `geomspace` also invalidates the supplied 1.1e-8 placement-error result; the source itself now claims a worst case of `2e-7`. [vertical.py:255](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:255) Re-run the reference sweep and either adapt quadrature resolution to width or enforce a minimum width.

- Both added `NamedTuple` fields break positional ABI by being inserted mid-tuple. An old positional `GridConfig(..., use_duogrid)` now assigns that boolean to `tropopause_refine`; every later positional `AMIPExperimentConfig` argument shifts. No in-repo positional consumer surfaced, but these are public serializable configs. Append fields at the end. [config.py:46](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:46), [amip_config.py:20](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/tools/legoesm/forcing/amip_config.py:20)

Assessment of supplied findings:

- F1: confirmed originally. The new projection fixes the pure-sigma MPAS arm, but not hybrid as above. Existing tests still only test the unweighted path, so they do not test this fix. [test_mpas_vertical_checkerboard.py:141](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/tests/unit/test_mpas_vertical_checkerboard.py:141)
- F2: fixed in the current worktree. The legacy schema and both adapters now carry the field. [amip_config.py:35](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/tools/legoesm/forcing/amip_config.py:35), [config.py:2392](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:2392), [config.py:2615](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:2615) Add a flat-AMIP checkpoint round-trip test.
- F3: partly fixed only for newly written MPAS checkpoints; see restart issues above.
- F4: capping at 3 rather than 6 is reasonable as an experimental allow-list, not a numerically justified safety bound. Refine=3 already violates the stated 1.2–1.3 smoothness practice. Require an explicit post-construction minimum-thickness and adjacent-ratio check; do not claim a universal “right” ratio without a stability study. [config.py:1307](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/config.py:1307)
- F5: narrow claim confirmed: sigma advection uses `dsigma_full`, so your stated advective CFL is the relevant one. [vertical.py:490](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:490) The blanket claim is false: Bechtold has a `dp/(g*dt)` mass-flux CFL cap, GWD computes stress divergence over `rho*dz` before limiting, and microphysics sedimentation has `Vt*dt/dz` CFL behavior. [bechtold.py:1725](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/convection/bechtold.py:1725), [hines.py:280](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/gravity_wave_drag/hines.py:280), [output.py:145](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/microphysics/output.py:145) They are capped/positivity-limited, so this does not establish the L40 cause.
- F6: the helper comment is now appropriately cautious, but stale causal claims remain in the CLI and test file. [run_amip.py:1282](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/run/run_amip.py:1282), [test_tropopause_refined_sigma.py:62](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/tests/unit/test_tropopause_refined_sigma.py:62)

Uniform-grid hunt:

- No issue in sigma-dot, vertical advection, plev interpolation, radiation layer construction, or hard saturation: they use `dsigma`, physical pressure interfaces, or local pressure correctly. [vertical.py:423](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:423), [diagnostics.py:590](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/diagnostics.py:590), [radiation/integration.py:985](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/radiation/integration.py:985), [model_driver.py:336](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/model_driver.py:336)
- Bechtold’s physical reductions use `dp_full`; its LCL/LNB soft gates use level index, so refinement changes their physical transition width. That is a tuning/non-invariance risk, not a demonstrated conservation bug. [bechtold.py:2082](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/convection/bechtold.py:2082), [bechtold.py:2186](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/atmosphere/legoesm/atmosphere/physics/convection/bechtold.py:2186)
- The MPAS qv smoother is pre-existing non-conservative with horizontally varying `p_s`, but refinement does not introduce that defect because it smooths each level independently. [model_driver.py:242](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/model_driver.py:242)
- Surface/ice/land use the actual lowest sigma level. They are not assuming uniform spacing, but the 30% thicker bottom layer changes their effective lower-layer response and needs retuning assessment. [physics_pipeline.py:1405](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/coupler/legoesm/driver/physics_pipeline.py:1405)

The new test file is weak: it does not pin refined interfaces, tests only one pressure/nlev/refinement, permits the top-layer flat-density mutant, claims “uniform gives 2” while asserting 4, and does not cover config/CLI, AMIP serialization, restart rejection, weighted del4 conservation, float32 monotonicity, or JIT/grad with a frozen refined coordinate. [test_tropopause_refined_sigma.py:28](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/tests/unit/test_tropopause_refined_sigma.py:28), [test_tropopause_refined_sigma.py:126](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/tests/unit/test_tropopause_refined_sigma.py:126)

Mathematically, sigma-space equidistribution with a log-sigma Gaussian density is coherent. It is not a Gaussian density in `log(sigma)` measure, and it necessarily moves the endpoint layers too; “only steals from the mid-troposphere” is false. [vertical.py:207](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:207) Setup-time NumPy does not affect dycore `jit`/`grad`/`vmap` because the coordinate is frozen before stepping, and no config path makes refinement traced. The module-wide claim that all functions are JAX-compatible is now false for this helper and for non-default `create_sigma_coordinate`. [vertical.py:22](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/vertical.py:22)

`git diff --check` passes. I could not run pytest here: the available Python lacks NumPy/JAX and pytest is unavailable.
